To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

employees' affective organizational commitments are positively related to their willingness to discriminate against job applicants who are not similar to them on a relevant demographic dimension, and this relationship is mediated by submissiveness to the authority figures in the organization.

employees who have affective commitment to an organization are more likely to comply with an organizational authority's discriminatory decisions and that this effect is stronger for employees who have more submissive attitudes toward organizational authorities.
(a) authority figures' demographic prejudices led to employment discrimination and (b) this effect was stronger for more affectively committed employees.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of authority figures' demographic prejudices and followers' organizational commitment on the likelihood of employment discrimination.
the role of affective organizational commitment in explaining employment discrimination.
the role that authority figures play in employment discrimination and the role that followers' commitment to their organization plays in employment discrimination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
employment discrimination is a function of both the demographic preferences of the authority figures and the affective commitment of the followers.
affective organizational commitment moderates the relationship between authority figures' demographic preference for employees and employment discrimination.
the results of these two studies support the hypothesis that affective organizational commitment mediates the relationship between submissiveness to authority and employment discrimination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
employment discrimination is an organizational problem, not just a group problem.

employment discrimination is a function of the interaction between authority figures' demographic preference, followers' affective commitment to their organizations, and followers' submissiveness to authority figures.

affective organizational commitment is a strong predictor of submissiveness to authority, and submissiveness to authorities is a strong predictor for employment discrimination. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2005 APA, all rights reserved)
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizational commitment may be a key mechanism through which employment discrimination is perpetuated. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
employees who are committed to their organizations may be more likely than others to discriminate against job candidates based on their demographic attributes.

employees' affective organizational commitments may be a key mechanism that helps explain the role of organizational authorities in perpetuating employment discrimination. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
